description: IFC, the Industry Foundation Classes, is buildingSMART International's standardised digital description of the built environment, including buildings and civil infrastructure, published as ISO 16739-1:2024 and meant to be vendor-neutral. The schema codifies the identity and semantics, attributes (such as material, colour and thermal properties) and relationships (locations, connections, ownership) of objects like columns and slabs, abstract concepts such as performance and cost, processes such as installation and operation, and the people involved. It can describe physical components, mechanical and electrical systems, structural and energy analysis models, cost breakdowns and schedules, and is used to exchange models between architects, owners and contractors and to archive as-built information. Data can be encoded as STEP, XML or JSON. Coverage: any building or infrastructure project. Access: technical documentation on the buildingSMART site, updated September 2026. Licence: an open standard; the ISO edition is sold by ISO. Caveats: model quality and property completeness vary widely between authoring tools and projects. Simulation uses are extracting building geometry, systems and materials from BIM for energy, structural, evacuation and facility digital twins. Related records: IfcOpenShell and gbXML.
